Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

play dough noun

also playdough, Play-Doh, modelling clay, modeling clay

* our formation

* (our own formation) massa lūsōria

Our name, on the house pattern for toys (see toy version): massa, a soft lump, as of pitch or of cheese (Verg., Ov.), and in Church Latin dough. To shape it is fingere, the classical verb for modelling in wax or clay (fingere ē cērā, Cic. Verr. 2.4.30). Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for it.

Other words

  • argilla, argillae f. — clay, for modelling

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 35.151; Cic. Pis. 59: ex argillā et lutō fictus (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Potter’s clay.

Examples

  • Ex massā lūsōriā anguem fingāmus.

    Let’s make a snake out of the play dough.composed

  • Fingere ex argillā similitūdinēs Būtadēs Sicyōnius figulus prīmus invēnit Corinthī

    Butades, a potter from Sicyon, was the first to model likenesses in clay, at CorinthPlin. NH 35.151

See also dough, knead, toy version, mould.

SourcesLewis & Short: massa · Lewis & Short: lusorius · Lewis & Short: argilla · Lewis & Short: fingo

Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for play dough (searched under play dough, playdough, clay, modelling clay, plasticine, and Italian plastilina, creta).
